overview: A mobile-first thermal engineering workbench for high-altitude military shelters that pulls live climate data, decomposes shelter geometry, simulates 24-hour heat loss, and returns a cost-versus-fuel design verdict.
features: Pick a high-altitude sector or coordinates and pull live NASA POWER weather plus elevation
Compute altitude-corrected air density for thin-air sites
Upload STL or OBJ shelter models and get floor, roof, and wall areas with interior volume
Run a 24-hour transient thermal simulation with wind, solar, infiltration, and permafrost effects
Get a dew-point breach alert when condensation risk appears
Explore a 125-configuration Pareto front trading cost against kerosene burn
Read operational verdicts: kerosene litres per day, comfort index, structural weight, airlift sorties, and sapper man-hours
Save and reopen analyses, and export a shareable report
Works offline with pre-compiled seasonal climate profiles for four sectors
